pageCache.pageTitle: Our Values and Drivers – Grangefield School
pageCache.text:
At Grangefield, our values are lived not just laminated. Our values help to shape what we deliver at school and shape the expectations we have of all those involved in the school community.
Our Values and Drivers
At Grangefield School we have high expectations of all our children. We are committed to educating in a holistic way focusing on the social, moral, creative and artistic as well as the academic. We hold six core values close to us and embed these values into everything we do.
Curriculum Drivers

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Grangefield School – Grangefield School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Grangefield School
On behalf of staff, pupils, parents, and governors, I would like to extend a warm welcome to Grangefield School and our website.
At Grangefield, we are dedicated to providing a safe, happy, secure, and supportive environment where all children can thrive and succeed. We take pride in our school and everything it represents.
Pupils are very proud to belong to this school and enjoy celebrating their own and others’ success. Staff are exceptionally proud to work at the school. Ofsted 2023
Our goal is to instill a love for learning in our pupils through engaging and enriching experiences. Our curriculum is designed to be broad, balanced, and stimulating, incorporating a variety of learning activities to cater to the diverse needs of our pupils.
Our school motto, ‘Flying high. Spreading our wings’, encapsulates our belief that every child has the potential to excel and be prepared for the future.
‘Flying high. Spreading our wings’ is the deeply embedded motto at Grangefield Primary School. Leaders and staff want the very best for their pupils. Ofsted 2023
We firmly believe that a strong partnership between home and school is essential for the holistic development of our pupils. This website serves as a gateway to keep you informed about the happenings at our school and we hope it provides you with a valuable insight into what we offer.
If you have any further questions or require additional information after exploring our website, please do not hesitate to reach out to us. We are always happy to assist and provide you with the information you need.
Thank you for visiting our website, and we hope you enjoy learning more about Grangefield School.
Gemma KyddHeadteacher

Personal Development
At Grangefield we recognise that the personal development of pupils, spiritually, morally, socially and culturally plays a significant part in their ability to learn and achieve. We therefore aim to provide an education that provides children with opportunities to explore and develop their own values and beliefs, spiritual awareness, high standards of personal behaviour, a positive caring attitude towards other people, an understanding of their social and cultural traditions and an appreciation of the diversity and richness of other cultures.
We use our owl family time for this as well as embedding this throughout all aspects of school life. You can see how SMSC if promoted across the curriculum in our ‘SMSC Curriculum Overview’
Our ‘Gaining My Wings’ awards allow families to continue this learning at home.
It is our intention to provide pupils with a range of exciting learning opportunities, both in and outside the classroom, with the support of our local community, which enable them to develop the attitudes and skills necessary for them to grow into responsible, happy and productive individuals and citizens.

pageCache.text:
Music Lessons at Grangefield
Instrumental lessons are a great way to not only engage your child in music making but are also proven to improve their confidence, concentration and much research has shown the positive effect of music on English and Maths in particular.
At Grangefield a range of external music lesson providers come into school and provide solo and group tuition before and after school, and during the school day.
Not owning an instrument should not be a barrier to learning to play – instruments can be hired from Gloucestershire music, and children who are receive Free School Meals are entitled to free instrument hire. Find out more here: https://www.gloucestershiremusic.co.uk/instrument-hire/ We will also support with the cost of tuition for those children eligible for Pupil Premium Funding.
Please see the information below about our peripatetic music teachers and the links to their individual information letters.
Name and Tuition Offered:
Rosy Crocker – Flute and Clarinet (Yr3-6), Saxophone (Y6)
Rosy has been teaching woodwind in Gloucestershire primary schools for around 15 years. She also plays with a group (as woodwind specialist) on Wednesdays at the Cotswold School in term time called North Cotswold Wind Band which has players of a wide range of ages and schools playing at fetes in the summer and Stow on the Wold Christmas Tree Festival. They play a variety pieces from James Bond to Shrek.
Ollie Heath – Violin
Ollie began playing the violin aged four, and went on to study at the Purcell School, Royal Northern College of Music, Guildhall School of Music and Drama, and the National Music Conservatoire in Madrid. He spent twenty years leading The Heath Quartet with whom he toured around the world, playing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Southbank Centre, Berlin Konzerthaus and Adelaide Arts Festival. Ollie has collaborated with many leading pop musicians and producers including Damon Albarn, The Who, Sam Smith and Dua Lipa. He has also been featured on many film soundtracks.
Alongside his playing career, Ollie has developed a love of teaching and has twenty years, experience teaching all levels of violin and chamber music students. He grew up learning the Suzuki method which has a big influence on his teaching style, but he firmly believes in the uniqueness of each student and responding to the myriad of different learning styles in a spontaneous way.
Music Guru – Piano, Guitar and Ukuele
The Music Guru is a small Gloucestershire based Music Tuition company, specialising in rock and pop. Pete Sen and the team are all performers and highly experienced teachers. They’re ready to get you to where you want to be. With a 100% pass rate you know you’ll be getting the best tuition possible. Students from ages 6 and up are all welcome!
Rocksteady – Electric guitar, bass, drums, keyboard and vocal
Rocksteady is the UK’s leading rock school and we’re proud that their fun, inclusive band lessons take place at our school. As well as teaching new musical skills through contemporary rock and pop music, Rocksteady have a proven significant, positive impact on wellbeing, confidence and life skills for primary aged children. Recently, they were awarded ‘Schools Wellbeing Resource of the Year’ at the Education Today awards, for their work inspiring children through music.

Reading is like a holiday in your head.
Reading at Grangefield
The Department for Education states:
‘Children do not just ‘become’ readers, however, and reading engagement is not possible if children struggle with the basic mechanics of reading. Fluency and enjoyment are the result of careful teaching and frequent practice. Ensuring children become fluent and engaged readers at the very earliest stages also helps avoid the vicious circle of reading difficulty and demotivation that makes later intervention more challenging.’
When our children leave Grangefield Primary School we expect them to be avid readers, children who read fluently and widely and are able to express preferences and opinions about the texts that they read. We want them to read for pleasure, having had access to a wide range of text types, genres and authors in order for them to make informed opinions about their favourites.
We aspire for every child at Grangefield to love reading!
Phonics
At Grangefield Primary School we have introduced the highly successful Ruth Miskin Read Write Inc phonics programme to teach our children to read, write and spell. As part of our driver for ‘Solid Foundations’ our aim is to ensure that our children become competent at spelling and fluent at reading, giving them the best possible start to their Reading and Writing journey.
All children who are reading the RWI storybooks in their class lessons will bring these ‘Teaching Books’ home as well as a Book Bag Book which exactly matches the sounds learnt in the session. The children will be able to read these books independently but it is important that you listen to your child read these books several times so that they build up their fluency and expression. In addition to these books they will bring home a library book of their choice which will be above their reading level therefore it is important that you share the reading of this book with your child.
“I don’t think there’s a big secret about what to do; we need to show children how much we love stories. Read great stories, poems and non-fiction every day, all through school. What we love today they might read tomorrow.” Ruth Miskin

Our Curriculum
Curriculum Intention
The Curriculum is all the learning and experiences, formal and informal, which a school provides for pupils. Our aim is to give our pupils an education that is exciting and worthwhile, prepares them for life beyond school, and lays the foundations for lifelong learning. In meeting these aims we have four school drivers:
Underpinned by our school values (including British values) and our curriculum drivers, our academic curriculum uses either the EYFS or the National Curriculum as the basis for content and expectations.
The breadth of our curriculum is designed with the following intention:
It is with these drivers, values and our curriculum objectives, that we are able to plan effectively to deliver an all-encompassing and balanced education for our children.
curiosity;
independent thinking and reasoning;
ability to apply knowledge and skills;
enjoyment and fascination;
imagination and creativity;
Curriculum Implementation
We plan our curriculum ensuring we meet the requirements of the National Curriculum and the Early Years Curriculum, and by focussing on our curriculum drivers. We plan the curriculum carefully, so that there is coherence and full progression in its coverage. Our school curriculum is underpinned by our principle value of providing high quality educational experiences that are focused on continued improvement in whole school standards and the development of independent, responsible and resilient learners.
Our curriculum design is based on evidence from cognitive science; three main principles underpin it:1) Learning is most effective when spaced rather than blocked.2) Interleaving helps pupils to discriminate between topics and aids long-term retention3) Retrieval of previously learned content is frequent and regular, which increases both storage and retrieval strength.
Most of our content is subject specific, but we make relevant links with prior learning and learning in other subjects as subject specific knowledge can be mutually reinforcing. We make it clear to the children what they are learning within a subject and how this knowledge fits in with their existing understanding.
We have structured this so that:a) Each year group has a clear list of what must be covered (long term planning)b) Each subject has a clear overview of what is taught and when (curriculum progression maps and subject overviews)c) We have clearly defined end points against which the children are assessed (using National Curriculum and National Assessment Frameworks)
To find out more about each curriculum subject please see subject overviews.
By law Religious Education must be taught according to the locally agreed syllabus in all maintained schools therefore we follow the Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for RE 2017-2022. Religious Education does not seek to urge religious beliefs on children or to compromise the integrity of their own beliefs by promoting one religion over another.
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
The Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education (England) Regulations 2019, made under sections 34 and 35 of the Children and Social Work Act 2017, make Relationships Education compulsory for all pupils receiving primary education. At Grangefield RSE is taught within the personal, social, health and economic (PSHE) education curriculum. Biological aspects of RSE are taught within the science curriculum, and other aspects are included in religious education (RE). You can find our RSE policy here.
Promoting British Values at Grangefield School
At Grangefield School, the children and their learning are at the very heart of every decision made. We aim to develop learners who are passionate, take ownership of their learning and are proud of their achievements. The school has three drivers: Good To Be Me, Solid Foundations and The Global Child. More information about promoting British values at Grangefield School can be found here.
Special Educational Needs
We believe that all of our children are special and endeavour to provide the best possible education for each of them. In line with national practice we have a special needs co-ordinator and a governor responsible for special needs within the school. If a child is identified as having needs that require additional provision they are placed on to the Gloucestershire Graduated Pathway of Support. Parents are notified before any child is placed on the pathway and are kept fully informed of their child’s progress. The whole team around each child work together to support them and ensure that they can succeed and thrive at Grangefield school.

Frequently Asked Questions
We hope that you find the information you’re looking for throughout the pages of our website. Below are answers to a few frequently asked questions. If you can’t find the information you’re looking for, please give the school office a call on 01242 671003 and the team will be able to help. If you need a paper copy of any of the information on the website just let the school office team know.
If your child needs to see the doctor, dentist etc we ask that whenever possible you make appointments outside of school time. When this is not possible please email or call the office to make the school aware.
If your child is ill please let the school know as soon as possible by either calling the school office or sending us an email. We can then let the teacher know and your child will not be marked down as having an unauthorised absence.
If you would like to help in our classrooms please have a word with your child’s teacher or the Head Teacher. We often need help and would be only too pleased to ‘find you a job’. Please bear in mind that if you do offer to help the teacher will plan accordingly.
If someone else will be collecting your child from school please ensure that you let the school know. You could speak to your child’s teacher, put a note in their book bag or call/email the school office.
Each year group has a class assembly each year that parents are invited to attend. The dates for these will be circulated in our newsletter and also included in our calendar.
Sports Day information and information about performances will be included in our newsletter, emails will be sent out and dates will be available on our calendar.
Class assemblies begin at 2:50pm.
You can find information about the individual start time for clubs on the calendar section of the website. Before school clubs finish at 8:45am. All teacher led after school clubs start straight after school at 3:15pm and finish at 4:15am.
At Christmas, Easter and when the summer holidays start school will finish at 2pm. For all other half terms school will finish at 3:15pm as normal.

pageCache.pageTitle: Grangefield School Ofsted Report – Grangefield School
pageCache.text:
Our teachers push us to come out of our comfort zone.
Grangefield School Ofsted Report
Grangefield Primary School: Ofsted Inspections Affirm Our Commitment to Excellence
Grangefield Primary School is dedicated to providing an exceptional educational experience for its pupils. Guided by our vision of “Flying High, Spreading Our Wings” and our core values of Respect, Determination, Friendship, Responsibility, Excellence, and Honesty, we strive to nurture the growth and development of every child in our care.
We have had two Ofsted inspections in the past two years. We are incredibly proud of both reports which are available to read using the links on this page and via the Ofsted website.
Graded Inspection: Achieving “Good” in All Areas
In July 2024, Grangefield was visited by Ofsted for a graded Ofsted inspection, where we were proud to be awarded a “good” rating in all areas. This achievement is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our entire school community, including our pupils, parents, and staff.
The inspection report highlighted our school’s strengths, noting our strong leadership, effective teaching practises, and the excellent progress made by our pupils. The inspectors were particularly impressed by the positive relationships fostered within the school, as well as our commitment to promoting the personal development and well-being of every child.
Ungraded Inspection: Continued Success
In January 2023, the school underwent an ungraded Ofsted inspection. The inspectors found that the school continues to be a “good” school, with enough evidence of improved performance to suggest that the school could be judged “outstanding” if a graded inspection were to be carried out.
This ungraded inspection affirms our commitment to maintaining and enhancing the quality of education we provide. Our dedicated team of teachers and staff work tirelessly to ensure that our pupils receive a well-rounded, enriching educational experience that aligns with our school’s values.
Continuous Improvement and Commitment to Excellence
At Grangefield Primary School, we are committed to a culture of continuous improvement and excellence. While we are delighted with the outcomes of our recent Ofsted inspections, we recognise that there is always room for growth and development.
We will continue to work closely with our pupils, parents, and the wider community to identify areas for improvement and implement strategies that will further enhance the quality of education we provide. By upholding our vision and values, we are confident that Grangefield Primary School will continue to thrive and inspire our pupils to achieve their very best.
If you have any questions or would like to learn more about our school, please do not hesitate to contact us. We welcome the opportunity to engage with our community and share our passion for education.

Keeping Children Safe
Keeping Children Safe – Our Core Purpose
We believe that one of the key roles of our school is to provide a caring, positive, safe and stimulating environment which promotes the social, physical and moral development of every individual child in our care, so that they grow up secure, confident and independent.
It is clear, therefore, that the health, safety and well-being of all the children in our care are of paramount importance. Our pupils have the right to protection, regardless of age, gender, race, culture or disability.
We recognise that all staff members have a full and active part to play in protecting our pupils from harm.
The first point of contact for anyone who has a concern about the safety and well-being of a pupil is the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL).
All concerns regarding child protection issues in school should be referred to Mrs Kydd in the first instance. This responsibility extends to every member of our community and it is of vital importance that all concerns are reported in confidence without delay to the Safeguarding Team.
Allegations Management
In order to manage allegations against child care professionals, every Local Authority appoints a Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO). In Gloucestershire the LADO can be contacted on 01452 426994 or amadmin@gloucestershire.gov.uk
Further information and advice can be obtained from the Gloucestershire Safeguarding Children Board or from our Safeguarding Policy.
